newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Credito stake in trusteeship.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Credito stake in trusteeship.

text.p: Banco de Credito Argentino, controlled by Argentina's Banco Frances, said Thursday shareholder Fernando de Santibanes transferred the fiduciary property of 32.3 million shares equivalent to about 16.42 percent of Credito's shareholders equity.
The deal was closed June 3 and the fiduciary agent is Banco Frances Cayman Ltd, Credito told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
Santibanes has a 28 percent stake in Credito.
Frances, controlled by Spain's Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya, last month bought 71.8 percent of Credito for $466 million.
According to local media reports, Bilbao's officials said Frances wanted to buy all the shares owned by Santibanes.
Bilbao also has interests in Mexico, Colombia and Peru.

NOTE: Makes clear shareholder Santibanes is not selling a 16.42 stake, as erroneously reported by Reuters, but constituting a trusteeship, which does not imply transfer of property of the shares, but their administration.
